oracle.tool: tools/java-oracle/Check.java (JavacTask.parse), run with the JDK single-file source launcher
oracle.dialect: Java, the JDK's own latest source level (21)
oracle.note: javac's own parser, stopped after PARSE so no attribution, no classpath resolution and no annotation processing happen; a missing dependency is not an error. Verified on 1000 files ripped out of their source trees with no classpath: 1000 valid. The JDK version is the source level and is load-bearing the way an interpreter version is elsewhere.

corpus.source: Maven Central top-100 by dependent repositories (ecosyste.ms index of repo1.maven.org), fetched 2026-08-06; each artifact's -sources.jar at the version maven-metadata.xml calls <release>; .java files
corpus.source_note: Maven Central publishes no download counts, so the ranking is a dependency-graph proxy (how many public repos depend on the artifact) rather than traffic, unlike the crates.io and npm rankings. 11 of the top 100 are pom-only aggregators with no sources jar and are skipped, leaving 89 artifacts.
corpus.oracle: tools/java-oracle — javac's own parser via com.sun.source.util.JavacTask.parse(), run through the JDK's single-file source launcher. Parse-only, so unresolved imports are not errors and each file is judged on its own, exactly like ts.createSourceFile for TypeScript. Requires a JDK; it exits nonzero rather than calling everything valid if none is present.

patches.title: type annotation before the varargs ellipsis
patches.origin: local; found by Maven top-100 sweep

evidence.spec: JLS 8.4.1 VariableArityParameter: {VariableModifier} UnannType {Annotation} ... VariableDeclaratorId — the annotations sit between the element type and the ellipsis. Upstream had repeat($._annotation) after the '...' instead of before it, so it rejected the legal form and accepted the illegal one; javac rejects `String ... @Nullable args`. Upstream's own corpus test asserted the illegal form, under the title "Annotations before a spread parameter's ellipsis" — the test source is corrected to match its title.

patches.title: `when` is a contextual keyword, not a reserved word
patches.origin: local; found by Maven top-100 sweep

evidence.repro: for (SimpleWhen when = this.when; when != null; when = when.next) {}
evidence.spec: JLS 3.9 lists `when` as a contextual keyword: it introduces a switch guard but stays a legal identifier everywhere else. Added to the grammar's existing _reserved_identifier list alongside `record`, `sealed`, `with` and `yield`. That makes `case x instanceof T when …` genuinely ambiguous — bind `when` as the instanceof pattern's name, or start the guard — so instanceof_expression is declared as a conflict and GLR keeps both readings alive.

patches.title: treebank crate identity
patches.origin: treebank; upstream owns the tree-sitter-java name on crates.io, so the redistribution publishes under its own: package name, repository, homepage and description. [lib] name stays upstream's so the crate is a drop-in. include gains LICENSE, ledger.json, LOCAL-PATCHES.md and patches/* so provenance travels inside the published tarball. Also fixes two defects that would otherwise ship: upstream's include omits LICENSE (an unlicensed redistribution), and the dev-dependency on tree-sitter 0.24 cannot load the ABI-15 parsers the pinned CLI 0.25.10 generates. The published version string is deliberately NOT here: publish.sh derives it from crates.io at publish time. See PUBLISHING.md.
